name: quickstart
description: A daily outdoor-temperature plot with a six-hour forecast. Judge only content inside the plot; ignore headings, descriptions, buttons, controls, and other surrounding UI.

checks.expectation: One coherent temperature plot is visible. Its axes, grid, curves, markers, and legend stay within the plot area without unintended overlap or clipping. Do not evaluate content outside the plot.

The Time of day (h) and Temperature (°C) axes, their tick labels, and a legend naming Outdoor temperature and Six-hour forecast are visible and readable. Assess only text presence and readability in this check; do not judge legend symbols or marker geometry.
A smooth solid outdoor-temperature curve spans the full day, rising from cooler values to a daytime high and then falling.

A visually distinct dashed forecast line and several visible markers appear in the plot and broadly follow the daily temperature trend. Exact marker shape, size, edge profile, count, position, and legend-symbol geometry are not evaluated at this screenshot scale. Do not fail because a marker appears round, square, clipped, partial, or different from the legend sample. Fail only if the forecast line or all of its markers are missing, clearly corrupted, or not distinguishable from the other series.

Within the plot, axis titles, tick labels, and legend text are readable and free of clear raster corruption. Fail only for concrete defects such as square pixel blocks, doubled glyphs, or severe stair-step edges that make plot text materially illegible. Do not compare plot text with headings, descriptions, buttons, controls, or any text outside the plot. Normal antialiasing, small fonts, rotated text, and backend-specific softness are acceptable.
Both curves, markers, axes, grid, labels, and legend are distinguishable; the plot is not blank, corrupted, or clipped.
